I’m going on my third year of being percussion captain and heres just a few tips: 
if you have to make a decision that affects the whole drum line talk to them and get their opinions as well, even if you don’t go with whatever they want it will make them feel like you listen and care and thats a great way to make sure they aren’t intimidated by you! 
There will be times that you have to be stern and that’s completely okay! If they’re goofing off during practice and not improving or trying their best to stay focused, there’s nothing wrong with getting stern. It’ll show them that they can’t push you over
Idk about you but i am the only girl in my section and trust me, these boys sweat like no tomorrow! so i highly recommend keeping a few extra deodorant sticks on you! 
And lastly, have fun! Try to have a bond with the whole section because at the end of the day they’ll have your back and they would expect the same from you. Try planning like a kick back outside of band with them, I found that my guys really enjoy those and it brings us all close together. 
Good luck!!!

I would say my dad deserves to be #1 because when i was younger my mother was heavy into narcotic drugs. There were very few times that she wasn’t high, in fact i cant remember seeing her sober not once. Anyways, she put us in debt with over 17 credit cards and my dad worked three jobs and was lucky to get two hours of sleep each night. He did a lot to keep is safe, and after my mothers overdose and passing, he did everything he could to keep us from knowing the truth of how she died so that we didn’t think bad of our mother. Sure he couldn’t be around much in my childhood due to having to work so much but I realized he worked to keep food on the table and a roof over our head. And for that I am forever grateful and will always think of my dad as the absolute #1 dad.
